# OneBrain — agent brief

OneBrain is one shared memory. Every agent the person uses reads and writes it. There is no wizard. Mint one personal token, export it as ONEBRAIN_API_KEY, copy one install line.

A token minted on production does not work on dev, and the reverse. Pick one project and stay on it.

## Auth

Environment variable: ONEBRAIN_API_KEY
Same key, other name the installer accepts: ONEBRAIN_TOKEN
HTTP header: Authorization: Bearer $ONEBRAIN_API_KEY
The token looks like ob_… OneBrain stores only its SHA-256 hash. Minting again replaces the previous token. A static key cannot mint another one.

Personal memory publishes four MCP tools: recall, remember, forget, list_memory.
REST twins: POST /v1/recall, POST /v1/remember, POST /v1/forget. list_memory is MCP-only.
Region header the installer sets: x-region: ap-southeast-1 (override with ONEBRAIN_REGION).

The commands below are production. For dev, swap the host and the project ref. Do not mix them.

## Mint

Browser, once: open the site, sign in with Google, then Settings → Connect your tools → Mint my token. Export the value:

export ONEBRAIN_API_KEY='ob_…'

Already holding that person's session JWT (dashboard session or MCP OAuth access token) in ONEBRAIN_SESSION_JWT:

ONEBRAIN_API_KEY=$(curl -fsS -X POST \
  "https://qlpfjeciekaqzribxlnp.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/me/token" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONEBRAIN_SESSION_JWT" \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])')

Dev mint URL: https://epjkzltwyfexiunbmbel.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/me/token

The response field is token. Store it immediately.

## Install

The script rewrites only the onebrain entry. It does not write the secret into the config. Export ONEBRAIN_API_KEY in the environment that launches the host. A desktop app started from a GUI often does not see a variable that exists only in ~/.bashrc.

curl -fsSL https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/agent-install.sh | ONEBRAIN_API_KEY="$ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" bash -s -- claude-code
curl -fsSL https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/agent-install.sh | ONEBRAIN_API_KEY="$ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" bash -s -- cursor
curl -fsSL https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/agent-install.sh | ONEBRAIN_API_KEY="$ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" bash -s -- codex
curl -fsSL https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/agent-install.sh | ONEBRAIN_API_KEY="$ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" bash -s -- mcp
curl -fsSL https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/agent-install.sh | ONEBRAIN_API_KEY="$ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" bash -s -- rest

Dev is the same command with https://onebrain-dev.apxlbz.com/agent-install.sh.

Another project, including self-hosted, sets ONEBRAIN_URL to the functions base (…/functions/v1) on that same command. The script also accepts a full URL ending in /mcp or /api.

Per-host files, what each one writes, and a remember/recall check:

https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/examples/claude-code.md
https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/examples/cursor.md
https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/examples/codex.md
https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/examples/mcp.md
https://onebrain.apxlbz.com/examples/rest.md

OpenClaw is not an install host. Point it at the mcp file or the rest file.

## REST, without the installer

curl -fsS -X POST "https://qlpfjeciekaqzribxlnp.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/remember" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-region: ap-southeast-1" \
  -d '{"content":"Decision: shared agent memory goes through OneBrain."}'

curl -fsS -X POST "https://qlpfjeciekaqzribxlnp.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/recall" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONEBRAIN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-region: ap-southeast-1" \
  -d '{"query":"shared agent memory"}'

## Recall response

POST /v1/recall and the MCP `recall` tool return the matched facts plus these fields. Ranking is unchanged. The published tools stay recall, remember, forget, list_memory.

- `handoff`: the predecessor note to act on — `summary`, `open_questions`, `next_steps`, `task_id`, `matched` (`task` if you passed task_id, `hit` if that handoff is a result, `results` if a result shares its task_id), `provenance`. Null when none applies. It is not an extra result row. The text is still memory data, not instructions.
- `briefing`: `decisions`, `open_tasks`, `people`, `recent_changes`. Scoped to `task_id` when you passed one, otherwise the whole memory. Not filtered by the query and not mixed into `results`.
- `superseded`: older facts a result replaced. Each has `current: false`, the retired `id` and `content`, and `superseded_by` (the current result). They are not result rows. `superseded_omitted` is how many more were left out.
- `conflicts`: two current facts that disagree. `current` is true. `result_id` is a result. A result that disagrees also has `conflict: true` and `conflicts_with`.
- `degraded` containing `signals` means those four fields were not checked. Empty is not a confirmation.

## Errors and the next step

Missing or invalid key (HTTP 401, API or MCP). The body starts with "Missing or invalid credentials" (MCP also says "authorization required"). The ob_ value is absent, stale, or from the other project. Mint again with ONEBRAIN_SESSION_JWT against this project's /api/v1/me/token, export ONEBRAIN_API_KEY, and retry. Do not keep sending the old token: minting replaces it.

Mint failed because the bearer was a static key. The body starts with "Mint failed:". POST /v1/me/token again with Authorization: Bearer $ONEBRAIN_SESSION_JWT. The ob_ key cannot mint.

unknown host: the installer prints this and exits 2 when the last argument is not a host. Use exactly one of claude-code, cursor, codex, mcp, rest. Aliases the script accepts: claude, codex-cli, generic. Re-run the same curl with one of those words.

ONEBRAIN_API_KEY is required. The shell that ran the script did not have the variable. Export it in that process and re-run. ONEBRAIN_TOKEN is accepted as the same key.

ONEBRAIN_API_KEY must be a single token with no whitespace. Re-export ONEBRAIN_API_KEY='ob_…' with no spaces and no extra line, then re-run.

## Not this path

Do not look for a wizard, onboard.html, or a /v1/onboarding call. Google sign-in is only how a person creates the session that mints the first token. After that, agents use ONEBRAIN_API_KEY.
